I've been on this land 20 years, and I've seen enough to know what works on my eight mu here in Quzhou. Let me think through this season carefully — my household has ten mouths, but several of the young ones earn wages outside, so the pressure on the fields is more about steady yield than squeezing every last kilo.

**Wheat first, since it's already in the ground from last October.** I planted Jimai 22 again — it's the improved variety the neighbors and I have trusted for years, good lodging resistance and handles our dry spring winds. I used about 12 kg/mu of seed. For fertilizer, I applied roughly 8 kg P₂O₅/mu and 5 kg K₂O/mu as base along with about 6 kg N/mu in diammonium phosphate and compound fertilizer at sowing. Now at spring greening/jointing I'll topdress another 10 kg N/mu as urea with the irrigation — so total N around 16 kg/mu. I used to put on 20+ kg N, but I've learned that was wasting money and the ear didn't get bigger; the extension station tested my soil two years back and it's already high in residual N from all the years of maize stover returned.

Irrigation: one winter water already done in December, then jointing water in late March, heading water in April, and grain-fill water in early May — four times total. Our well still pumps fine but electricity isn't free, so I don't water unless the top 10 cm is dry. Pesticide: one spray for aphids and powdery mildew combined at heading, one herbicide in early spring for thistle and bindweed. Two applications. Rotary tillage before sowing — ploughing every 3-4 years, this was a rotary year.

**Expected wheat yield: around 500 kg/mu.** Good years I get 550, bad dry springs 450.

**Then summer maize after wheat harvest in June.** I'll direct-seed Zhengdan 958 — hybrid, still the most reliable ear size for our heat and our planting date. About 2 kg seed/mu, plant density around 4,500 per mu. No tillage — I just run the no-till planter through the wheat stubble. This saves diesel and keeps the straw covering the soil through the hot spell.

Fertilizer for maize: 6 kg N/mu as base with the planter (compound 18-18-18 at 25 kg/mu gives me about 4.5 each of N-P-K), then topdress 12 kg N/mu at the big-trumpet stage (V10-12) when the ear is forming. So roughly 18 kg N/mu, 5 kg P, 5 kg K. Maize is the hungrier crop and rainfall in July-August usually gives me what I need for irrigation — but I'll put down one emergence water if June stays dry, and maybe one grain-fill water in August if the rains skip us. So 1-2 irrigations, call it 2.

Pesticide: one treatment for fall armyworm and corn borer combined at big-trumpet stage, plus one herbicide right after emergence for barnyardgrass. Two applications.

**Expected maize yield: around 600 kg/mu.** 

My thinking this year: I'm not changing much from last year because last year's yields were solid and maize prices are soft — no point gambling on more inputs. The money I save on fertilizer goes toward the electric pump repair and a bit set aside for my grandson's school.
